Appreciate the clear list — we can cover everything below and Ive looped in Neha (crypto ops) and Karthik (platform) for the technical attachments. High-level answers up front and attachments follow. If anything needs a deeper dive, we can schedule a 30-min call Monday.

Quick summary:
- BYOK import flow: we support customer-supplied key material via an encrypted import exchange. Customers upload a wrapped key and an import manifest to our control plane; the import is processed by a dedicated import workstation that uses an HSM-backed unwrap operation. We accept PKCS#8 (RSA/ECDSA) and raw symmetric AES keys wrapped with RSA-OAEP-256 or ECIES (Curve25519) per the import manifest.
- Validated HSMs: Thales Luna (7.x), SafeNet/Luna SA, and AWS CloudHSM have been validated for direct KMIP imports. For other vendors we support a KMIP-wrapped import model. Full compatibility matrix attached.
- Audit evidence: we can provide a redacted import audit snippet showing import_id, actor, timestamp, source_ip, wrapping_alg, cipher_hash, hsm_serial (redacted), and result. See attached redacted-import-audit-snippet.txt.
- Rotation & revocation: we recommend a 90-day rotation for symmetric keys used in customer workloads, with automated zero-downtime rollover using dual-target envelope keys. Emergency revocation is supported through immediate key state change (disabled) with cross-service TTL-based cache flush.
- TLS profile: minimum TLS 1.2, prefer TLS 1.3. Accepted ciphers: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 for legacy TLS1.2 endpoints. Forward secrecy enforced.

Im attaching: redwood-byok-stepguide.pdf (process + sequence diagram), hsm_integration_guide.pdf (vendor matrix & operational notes), and a redacted import audit snippet.

Next steps: well upload the full evidence set to a secure share and send the BYOK agreement for signature. If procurement prefers, we can do the import under a witness session with Cygnus ops.

Emily / team,

Adding a few implementation details so your security reviewers can validate against internal controls: 

- Import flow (detailed):
  * Customer generates key material in their environment and produces an import envelope using a locally held wrapping key (RSA-OAEP-256 or X25519-based ECIES).
  * The import envelope and manifest (JSON) are uploaded to a temporary, short-lived staging bucket. Uploads are authenticated by mTLS client certs and our API gateway validates the upload before granting a one-time import token.
  * A locked import host (air-gapped from production fabric) pulls the envelope using the one-time token. The import host uses an HSM to unwrap the envelope within an HSM-protected boundary; unwrapped keys are provisioned directly into the customer-dedicated key namespace and never persist on disk.
  * HSM attestation: for applied HSMs we capture an attestation blob (HW-provided quote) which we store alongside import metadata.

- Key formats accepted: AES-256 (raw), PKCS#8 private keys (PEM/DER), and JWK.SymmetricKey for JSON manifests.

- Operational controls: multi-person approval for imports to production (>1 approver), mandatory 30-day retention of import audit events in our primary audit store, and a separate immutable retention for compliance samples (WORM).

- Rotation details:
  * Soft-rotation window: rolling key activation where a new envelope key is introduced and both key versions are active for up to 72 hours to allow in-flight sessions to finish.
  * Hard cutover: after validation the old key is marked expired and scheduled for secure deletion under customer policy (30/90/365 day options).

- Revocation: revocation propagates via our distributed cache invalidation (sub-second TTL invalidation for critical keys) and we publish a key-state webhook to the customer's circuit for fast notification.

If you want a sample attestation blob or an example MI/Tenant policy, we can produce a redacted one. Suggest a technical call Monday 09:00 PT to walk through the import workstation sequence (15-20 min).

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Crypto Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attached is a redacted import audit (redacted-import-audit-snippet.txt) that matches the schema your SIEM team requested. Example fields included are import_id, customer_id, actor_email, import_timestamp, source_ip, wrapping_alg, hsm_vendor, hsm_serial (redacted), manifest_hash, and import_result. We also added an example attestation blob (see drive link) and a short design note on how split-key escrow can be implemented with Redwood:

Split-key escrow option (summary):
- Redwood supports a custodied escrow model where the import envelope is split into N shares using Shamirs Secret Sharing (configurable threshold). Shares are distributed across three escrow holders: (a) customer vault, (b) Redwood escrow service (HSM-backed), and (c) third-party auditor (mutually agreed).
- Reconstitution requires at least 2-of-3 shares (or threshold you choose) and is executed inside an HSM boundary with multi-party approval. We log and attestate every reconstitution event.
- For customers that require no Redwood access, we can support a witness-only import where Redwood performs the import operation in the customer's presence and the unwrapped keys are never retained by Redwood.

Ive uploaded the full evidence set to a secure share: https://drive.google.com/redwood/cygnus-byok-evidence and started a DocuSign for the BYOK addendum: https://docusign.com/tx/REDWOOD-CYG-BYOK-1123. Please review the redlined addendum and sign when ready. If you want us onsite for an observed import, we can provision a witness window the week of Aug 4.

Thanks — let us know if procurement needs any changes to the agreement language or if you want the attestation blob in a particular format.
